items.title: Danny Barker Interview, 1976-02-04
items.q: So he went into When You Smilin', he played it. And he didn't have a mic, but the band was real soft and he sang it.

ctx.x: Excuse me Danny, what was the name of the band you were with then?

I was with Lee Collins, Jones and Collins. Astoria Band. We played at Astoria. We played in New Orleans on Rampart Street which was owned by Beansy Furrier. It had once been owned by, I can't think of a man's name. It was a brewery people. Beansy took it over. It was a gambling concession. and we worked there. And Professor Cook was the emcee in musical and performance director and everything. He was the wheel around there. So he staged this train excursion to Chicago, and we had our band to play. items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Played with Louis . . . played a short tour with Louis Armstrong, through Virginia.

ctx.x: How did you first get in Cab’s band?

I’m around there, and I’m starting from the bottom. It’s 1930, with Harry White’s band. I’m with Dave Nelson’s band. I’m with Danny Logan’s band. I’m with Luis Russell’s band. Played with Louis . . . played a short tour with Louis Armstrong, through Virginia. Bill Johnson got drunk, and Luis Russell wanted to hire somebody else. Paul told him, “If you hire somebody else, I quit. Hire my nephew.” So he hired me. Bill Johnson got well again and then Bill Johnson got drunk again. They had to tolerate Bill. Bill…
This is not the same Bill Johnson that played with King Oliver.
